title: Apply Operations to Maximize Score
summary: Given an array of positive integers and an integer k, start with a score of 1.
statement: Given an array of positive integers and an integer k, start with a score of 1. Perform at most k operations by selecting a non-empty subarray, choosing an element with the highest prime score (or smallest index if ties), and multiplying the score by this element. The prime score is the count of distinct prime factors. Return the maximum score modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Prime score counts distinct prime factors.
Each subarray selects its leftmost maximum-prime-score element; use at most k distinct subarrays.
hints: Each index wins a rectangular set of subarrays bounded by greater-or-equal score on the left and strictly greater score on the right.
Use asymmetric monotonic stacks to count wins, then consume the largest numeric multipliers first.
Compute count=(i-left)*(right-i); sort (nums[i],count) descending and use up to k copies.
The boundaries encode the tie rule exactly, and choosing largest available factors maximizes a positive product.
editorial: The boundaries encode the tie rule exactly, and choosing largest available factors maximizes a positive product.

tests.explanation: Two subarrays can select nine, producing eighty-one.
Prime-score dominance counts and descending values identify the best three multipliers.
